Cerebellar, cardiac and skeletal malformations characterize the syndrome; chorioretinal coloboma in 2/2 supports ocular involvement. Evidence comes from very few patients.
Inherited degeneration of the vitreous and retina with common cataracts; disease is confined to the ocular axis.
Inherited copper homeostasis disorders; hepatic, neurologic and connective tissue damage vary across subtypes and cannot be generalized to the umbrella.
Chronic autoimmune cutaneous disease affecting skin and sometimes subcutis; systemic lupus manifestations are not intrinsic to this concept.
Menstrual cycle-linked fever without established organ injury or immune-mediated mechanism; occasional cortisol elevation does not establish endocrine disease.
Immune-mediated microscopic inflammation of the colon with subepithelial collagen deposition and chronic diarrhea.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the glottic larynx, which belongs to the airway axis.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common defining effects; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Biallelic GUCY2D-related retinal dysfunction or degeneration defines this retinopathy.
Skeletal deformities and mitral regurgitation each reported in 1/1; generalizability uncertain. Pneumonia, hypothyroidism and microcytic anemia may be separate conditions.
Congenital joint contractures and skeletal fusions define the disorder; pterygia alone do not establish additional skin injury.
Congenital abnormal motor pathway control produces involuntary mirror movements; there is no primary skeletal muscle disease.
Scarring causes inward rotation of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Bilateral congenital fusion of the humerus and ulna directly affects bones and elbow joints.
Primordial skeletal growth disorder with microcephaly, developmental delay and intellectual disability in 2/2; ectopic kidney in 1/2 does not establish renal impairment.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; gingival overgrowth 13/15, oligodontia 3/3 and hearing loss 6/12 support involvement. Neurologic findings in 1/1 lack representative frequency.
Inherited cardiac electrical dysfunction causing arrhythmias and conduction disorders; normal cardiac morphology does not negate functional disease.
Purine metabolic disorder; gout and uric acid stones are separately diagnosed consequences. Renal impairment occurs in only 5-29%; neurologic disease is not characteristic.
Frontotemporal and motor neuron degeneration define disease; muscle wasting and dysphagia result from denervation rather than primary muscle or gastrointestinal injury.
Hydrocephalus defines syndrome; urinary system anomalies occur in 80-99% and congenital cardiac defects in 30-79%. Nonspecific thoracic morphology adds no axis.
Neoplasm originates in the endocrine pituitary gland despite lacking a hormone-excess syndrome; visual injury is not established across this broad group.
Inflammation directly affects the orbital periosteum, involving ocular adnexa and skeletal tissue; infection or autoimmunity is not established.
Malignant epithelioid mesothelioma originates in the pleura.
Gastrin-secreting pancreatic endocrine tumor; acid-mediated gastroduodenal ulceration occurs in most patients and defines its Zollinger-Ellison functional syndrome.
